title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Jurisdictional Areas and Case Scope of Dalian, Wuhan, and Beihai Maritime Courts
keywords_en: Jurisdiction area and cases of maritime courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Adjusting the Jurisdictional Areas and Case Scope of the Dalian, Wuhan, and Beihai Maritime Courts

Fa [2002] No. 274

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and all maritime courts:

In order to meet the development of China's shipping economy and the needs of maritime adjudication, and in accordance with the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the jurisdictional areas and case scope of the Dalian Maritime Court, the Wuhan Maritime Court, and the Beihai Maritime Court are hereby adjusted as follows:

1. The jurisdictional area of the Dalian Maritime Court covers: the extended sea areas from the boundary between Liaoning Province and Hebei Province in the south to the mouth of the Yalu River in the east, and the waters of the Yalu River, including a part of the Yellow Sea, a part of the Bohai Sea, offshore islands, as well as maritime and admiralty cases arising in the navigable waters connected to the sea, such as the Heilongjiang, Songhua, and Wusuli Rivers in Heilongjiang Province, and ports.

2. The jurisdictional area of the Wuhan Maritime Court covers: maritime and admiralty cases arising in the navigable waters connected to the sea and ports between the Hejiangmen in Yibin City, Sichuan Province, and the Liukou in Jiangsu Province.

3. The jurisdictional area of the Beihai Maritime Court covers: maritime and admiralty cases arising in ports, waters, the Beibu Gulf and its islands and waters under the jurisdiction of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, as well as in the navigable waters connected to the sea, such as the Lancang River to the Mekong River in Yunnan Province. The boundary between the jurisdictional areas of the Beihai Maritime Court and the Guangzhou Maritime Court is the center line of the Yingluo Bay channel; the area east of the center line and its extension is under the jurisdiction of the Guangzhou Maritime Court, and the area west of the center line and its extension, including the waters of Wuni Island, Weizhou Island, Xieyang Island, etc., is under the jurisdiction of the Beihai Maritime Court.

4. The Dalian Maritime Court, Wuhan Maritime Court, and Beihai Maritime Court shall respectively have jurisdiction over the following maritime and admiralty cases occurring within the waters of Heilongjiang Province (Dalian), the tributaries of the Yangtze River (Wuhan), and the waters of Yunnan Province (Beihai) as described above:
   (1) Cases of ship collision, general average, salvage, ship-source pollution, ship arrest and auction;
   (2) Foreign-related maritime and admiralty cases.
   Other maritime and admiralty cases occurring in the above waters shall be under the jurisdiction of the local people's courts.

5. When hearing maritime and admiralty cases, local people's courts shall apply the provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws.

December 10, 2002
